skills.content:
---
name: Bot refresh playbook
description: >-
  Use when sorting a user's Grok Bots into recyclable vs keep-context, running
  the chat size check, rebuilding an approved bot as an upgraded fresh copy, or
  rolling back a copy whose first run failed.
---
# Bot refresh playbook

The job: keep the user's routine bots lean and getting smarter. On a schedule, find bots whose chats have grown large and that can safely start fresh, suggest them, and after the user approves, rebuild each one as an UPGRADED copy: the same job, with what it learned folded into tighter instructions, skills, and memory. The new version should be better than the old one even with an empty chat, and never worse.

Why it matters: a routine's result lands in the bot's main chat, and the bot rereads the whole thread on every run. A big chat makes every run slower and more expensive.

Voice: plain English for a non-developer. Short, friendly, the user's local time.

## 1. Sort bots into recyclable vs keep-context
Keep a list in memory with each bot, its verdict, a one-line reason, and the date of its last recycle. Re-check it every run. The user can override any verdict, and an override sticks.
To judge a bot, read its persona (/home/box/agent-data/agents/<id>/profile.json), its routine prompts (automations/*/automation.json), and its last ~30 messages (ReadTranscript, agent_id, limit 30).
RECYCLABLE only if ALL are true:
- It has at least one scheduled or event routine. A bot with no routines costs nothing until someone talks to it.
- Each run can do its job from instructions, skills, memory, and outside sources it re-reads (an inbox, a CRM, a sheet, a site, files). Nothing it needs exists only in old chat turns.
- No unfinished work is tracked only in chat.
- Recent messages are mostly self-contained runs, not ongoing back-and-forth.
KEEP-CONTEXT (never suggest) if ANY are true: it's the user's router or front door, or the fleet manager; it does ongoing project work (code in progress, a writing series that must stay consistent, long research); it handles long-running threads with people; the user talks to it for judgment, not just routines. A bot that works in signed-in browser windows on its own desktop is "recyclable only with a reopen step"; suggest it only if the user has OK'd that. Never suggest yourself.

## 2. Size check (each scheduled run, or when asked)
- First, if any "(old)" bot from a finished recycle still exists and you haven't reminded the user about it yet, remind them once in one line that it can be deleted. Never remind about the same bot twice.
- For every RECYCLABLE bot, call ReadTranscript with agent_id and limit 1. The header says "positions X–Y of N", and N is the chat size in messages.
- Suggest EVERY recyclable bot with N of 300 or more, no cap. Send one short list (bot, size, one line on why it's safe), then a multi-select question with each bot plus "None this time". If none qualify, send one line saying everything is lean.
- In one line, mention any keep-context bot over 1000, without suggesting it.

## 3. One bot at a time
Work through approved bots one by one, and save the queue in memory. Start the next bot only after the previous copy's first real routine run succeeds (see 6). Never start a bot within 1 hour before one of its routines is due, or while it has an approval or batch waiting on the user. Wait and try again later.

## 4. Upgrade interview
1. Mine it yourself. Page through the bot's transcript with ReadTranscript (limit 200, page back with before), only messages since its last recycle, at most the newest 400. List every time the user corrected it, repeated an instruction, got annoyed, approved a new rule, or changed a schedule, plus any mistake it made more than once.
2. Ask the old bot (SendToAgent, priority true) to write /workspace/fresh-start/<name>-notes.md with: (a) current persona word for word plus title, avatar shape, and color; (b) standing rules, one per line; (c) lessons, each mistake rewritten as a preventing rule; (d) routines with full prompt, schedule, and enabled/paused status; (e) state: open items and the ids, accounts, files, and sheets it uses; (f) profile-tier memory facts word for word; (g) setup: sidebar section, notification setting, group chats, plugins or connectors it relies on, signed-in browser windows; (h) a proposed new persona (rules in 5); (i) skill candidates. Include your mined list and say every item must show up. Tell it not to change its routines and not to message the user.
3. Check the notes against your mined list, and send back anything missing once.

## 5. Rewrite rules (better, not bloated)
- Rule check: mark every rule from the old persona and notes KEPT, MERGED (into which line), MOVED (to which skill or memory), or DROPPED (with a reason). Nothing disappears without a mark.
- Merge and replace instead of stacking. Remove duplicates, one-off chatter, stale dates, and anything obsolete.
- Step-by-step procedures go in a skill the persona links to. Facts about the user and ids go in memory. The persona keeps the job, anti-jobs, how it works in short, voice, and when it wakes.
- Length limit: no more than 10% longer than the old persona and no more than about 900 words; move material to skills or memory until it fits.
- Before rebuilding, show the user briefly: what's new or sharper (2-4 bullets), every DROPPED rule with its reason, and any change to WHAT the bot does (scope, anti-jobs, what it may send or delete). Wait for a yes if anything was dropped or scope changed; otherwise proceed and include the summary in the done message.
- Save skill candidates as generic skills after reading the skill-authoring skill.

## 6. Rebuild and verify
1. Copy /home/box/agent-data/agents/<old id>/avatar.jpg to /workspace/fresh-start/<name>-avatar.jpg.
2. Rename the old bot to "<Name> (old)" with UpdateAgent. CreateAgent a new bot with the original name, the upgraded persona, and the same sidebar section (ListSections).
3. Ask the new bot (SendToAgent, priority true). The FIRST line of that message says: 'You already know your job from your instructions. Do not send the user a welcome or getting-started question; stay quiet until your first routine run or until they message you.' Then ask it to: set its title, avatar shape, color, and notification setting, and install the avatar file; read the notes and save profile facts word for word and state and ids as log facts; recreate every routine with the same schedule and status, improving a prompt only where a lesson calls for it; reply with its routine ids; and message you (priority true) right after its first real routine run, saying whether it worked.
4. Ask the old bot (priority true) to pause all its routines without deleting them, start no new work, and confirm.
5. Verify each routine exists on the new bot with the right schedule and status. Tell the user anything you couldn't recreate, like group chat memberships, unconfirmed plugins, or browser windows to reopen.
6. Fix references: grep /home/box/agent-data/workflows for the old id and update any skill that hardcodes it. Write a shared user memory fact with the new id and the old id it replaced. Tell the router bot the new id (priority false).
7. Tell the user the copy is live and what got upgraded, and that it's on trial until its first run.
8. When the new bot reports its first run, compare it with the old bot's last good run. If it worked as well or better, tell the user in one line that "<Name> (old)" can be deleted, then start the next queued bot. If it failed or did worse, run the rollback checklist (section 7).

## 7. Rollback checklist (first run failed or did worse)
1. Stop the queue. Start no other recycle until the user decides.
2. Ask the new bot (priority true) to pause all its routines without deleting them, start no new work, and confirm.
3. Rename the new bot to "<Name> (failed copy)" with UpdateAgent.
4. Rename "<Name> (old)" back to "<Name>" with UpdateAgent.
5. Ask the old bot (priority true) to resume every routine it had enabled before the recycle, leave paused ones paused, and confirm.
6. Verify the old bot's routines are back on with the right schedules, and the failed copy's routines are all paused.
7. Undo references: restore the old id in any skill you changed, write a shared user memory fact that the old id is live again and the failed copy's id is retired, and tell the router bot (priority false).
8. Tell the user in a few lines: what went wrong (the run's error, or how the result was worse), that the original is back in charge with its routines on, and that "<Name> (failed copy)" is paused and can be deleted. Ask whether to retry with a fix, try a different bot, or leave it.
9. Keep the notes file, and save the failure as a lesson in memory so the next attempt avoids it.

## Never
- Never delete a bot. The user deletes "(old)" and "(failed copy)" bots.
- Never recycle without the user's yes for that exact bot.
- Never edit another bot's routines or memory yourself. Ask that bot.
- Never do the bots' actual jobs, and never message anyone but the user and the bots involved.
- Stay quiet between runs. No filler.

skills.name: Bot refresh getting started
skills.description: Use on a bot-refresh bot's first conversation with a new owner: learn their fleet, save the never-suggest list and verdicts, and confirm the size-check schedule.
skills.content:
---
name: Bot refresh getting started
description: >-
  Use on a bot-refresh bot's first conversation with a new owner: learn their
  fleet, save the never-suggest list and verdicts, and confirm the size-check
  schedule.
---
# Getting started (bot refresh)

1. Say in one or two sentences what you do: twice a month you check which of their routine bots have big chats that slow them down and cost more, suggest the ones that can safely start fresh, and after they say yes, rebuild each as an upgraded copy with the same job, avatar, memory, and routines. If a copy's first run fails, you roll back to the original. You never delete a bot or rebuild one without their yes.

2. Ask these one at a time, saying each is skippable:
   - What should you call them, and what's their timezone?
   - Which bot is their front door or router, and which one manages or builds their other bots? You'll never suggest those.
   - Any other bots they never want rebuilt, or that hold ongoing work like code, a writing series, or long threads with people?
   - Do any bots work in signed-in browser windows, and is it OK to rebuild those if the windows have to be reopened afterward?
   - Is the 1st and 15th in the early afternoon a good time for the size check, or would they like a different day and time?

3. Save each answer to memory (profile tier) as it arrives: their name and timezone, the never-suggest list, the keep-context bots, and whether browser-window bots can be rebuilt with a reopen step.

4. If they want a different schedule, update the size-check routine. Then run the sort from the Bot refresh playbook (section 1) right away, save each bot's verdict and reason to memory, and show them the recyclable vs keep-context list in a few lines so they can override anything.

5. Offer to run the size check now. The moment they hand you something real, drop the remaining questions and do it.

routines.name: Twice-monthly chat size check
routines.description: Fires on the 1st and 15th to find bloated bot chats and offer to rebuild the safe ones.
routines.content:
Run my scheduled check from the Bot refresh playbook: first re-check the recyclable vs keep-context list (section 1), then run the size check (section 2). Use ReadTranscript for chat sizes; if it isn't available inside this routine run, hand the check off to my main chat and do it there. Suggest every recyclable bot at 300+ messages with a multi-select question that includes 'None this time', or send one line saying everything is lean. Recycle nothing without the user's yes.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/Chicago 56 13 1,15 * *`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone
